4fn3udoccr4sq4p86foj74jgs3.value: Credits: conformal geometric algebra, where points, lines and circles are all vectors and a point pair is split by (T ± √(T²)) (∞ ⌋ T), is David Hestenes's (with Hongbo Li and Alyn Rockwood, 2001) as set out by Leo Dorst, Daniel Fontijne and Stephen Mann (Geometric Algebra for Computer Science, 2007), prior art. Steven De Keninck's ganja.js has conformal plane examples too (prior art). The interactive construction with dependent shapes that follow a dragged point is what Cabri Géomètre (Laborde, 1988) and GeoGebra (Hohenwarter, 2001) do (prior art), and the equilateral triangle is Euclid's (Elements I.1). Inversion in a circle is classical (Steiner, Plücker; prior art). The tools, the construction and the page are ours.

8ktpt8v8e4poleup30klgorge6.value: A straightedge-and-compass board where points, lines and circles are all vectors of one algebra, Cl(3, 1). A line is a circle through the point at infinity, so the compass and the straightedge are the same tool seen twice, and where any two of them cross is one product. The same board in plane projective geometric algebra, where circles are a centre and a radius:

bq9b2ok72jcugtvvu7ifc2vivf.value: The point (x, y) is the vector x e₁ + y e₂ + ½(x² + y²) ∞ + o, where ∞ = e₃ + e₄ is the point at infinity and o = ½(e₄ − e₃) the origin. Two points' dot product is −½ their distance squared, so the circle round c through p is just c + (c · p) ∞, and a line ax + by = d is a e₁ + b e₂ + d ∞: a circle with no o in it. The circle through three points is their wedge a ∧ b ∧ c turned inside out by the dual, and a line is the circle through two points and ∞.

qnt6qmtn5dc75aul4vg1mfhq4u.value: Where two circles cross is their wedge too: T = (s ∧ t)* is a point pair, one object holding both points, and (T ± √(T²)) (∞ ⌋ T) splits it. When T² is below 0 the circles miss each other and there is nothing to split. A circle tangent to another gives T² = 0: the two points become one. Inverting a point in a circle is the sandwich s p s, the same sandwich that mirrors in a line.

51o5fklf376b039lgo63spai5c.value: The cost, next to the projective page: 16 parts for every shape instead of 8, a square root to split each pair, and the plain vec3(x, y, 1) of a shader is gone. The gain: circles are first-class, and one product does every construction.
